TASK-143 fixed Unified State decoding for historical integrated REMEDIATION failures. TASK-140 RUN-140-008 therefore became repairable and REPAIR-140-008 was executed as RUN-140-009 from failed integrated base 8ca93553393145549d9f6e8aef1477cc10ded845. The Executor produced a clean transportable candidate 9f893fc2eb56be0052fadae97e8b99099430085f whose only changed files relative to the failed head are .agents/aios_antigravity_pretool_guard.py and tests/test_antigravity_adapter.py, exactly the authorized FINDING-140-005 repair scope.
Runtime nevertheless failed RUN-140-009 at COMPLETION_GATE with "committed changed paths outside TASK.scope.modify" listing TASK-141/TASK-142 and Runtime files. The failure is deterministic: historical REPAIR admission preserves the original TASK root_base_sha 3002625fe0ca77e580925835445c6a9be3818fb5, and repair_completion_policy uses that root as result_base_sha. For a failed integrated REMEDIATION, however, the repair subject starts from the synthetic integration candidate 8ca935..., which intentionally carries canonical-main changes unrelated to TASK-140. Diffing original TASK root -> repaired candidate therefore attributes integration-carried files to the repaired TASK and rejects a valid correction.
Audit also shows the same legacy assumption exists downstream. Publisher's _repair_review_lineage still requires a failed REMEDIATION predecessor run.base_sha to equal remediation.reviewed_sha, which is false by design for integrated execution_base; and _validate_repair_package compares REPAIR RESULT.changed_files against root_base_sha. Brain Authoring Ingress SUBMIT_REVIEW still lacks the canonical REPAIR-of-REMEDIATION DELTA review reconstruction needed for this repaired correction path. Fixing only Runtime would therefore strand the same valid candidate at the next lifecycle boundary.
